article.Citation/Title: Johnson, F. G. (1969). LSD in the treatment of alcoholism. American Journal of Psychiatry, 126(4), 481-487.
article.SourcePDF: alcohol/Johnson, F. G. (1969). LSD in the treatment of alcoholism.pdf
article.InterventionDescription: Single IV LSD session, 300mcg (titratable to 500mcg+), hospital setting, with or without therapist present; single-blind; compared to amobarbital-methamphetamine or routine outpatient care.

article.Outcome: Table 4 gives two columns per criterion: pre/post significance 'taken across all treatment groups' and 'differences between treatment groups.' The primary hypothesis under test is whether LSD outperformed the other three arms, so the relevant comparison is the between-groups column, not the pooled pre/post column. Abstinence is the first-listed and most directly SUD-specific criterion in Table 4 and is treated as the primary outcome per the abstract's lead ('drinking'). No F-value, mean difference, or other magnitude statistic is given for the between-groups comparison anywhere in the article -- only the label 'NS' -- so no numeric or labelled-descriptor value exists to report and Outcome is coded '.'.
article.SD: No test statistic (F, t, chi-square) or dispersion value is reported for the between-groups Abstinence comparison; Table 4 shows only the qualitative tag 'NS' for that cell with no accompanying number or df. Coded '.'.
article.PVal: Table 4, 'Differences between treatment groups' row for Abstinence (and every other criterion) is printed literally as 'NS', with no numeric p-value given anywhere for the between-groups test. Recorded verbatim per the non-negotiable rule against converting NS to a number or threshold.
article.SampleSize_NFinal: Results state '[e]ighty-seven percent of the subjects in groups 1 to 4 were successfully followed up' (of 95 total), and this followed-up group is the one whose pre/post responses were compared via repeated-measures ANOVA. 87% of 95 = 82.65, which is not a clean integer, and the article never states the exact analyzed N or how non-integer attrition was handled. Rather than guess between 82 and 83, this is coded '.' per the instruction that an honest '.' is preferable to a fabricated number.

MethodologyDescribedYN.note: Objective, design (single-blind 4-arm design), setting (London Clinic), eligibility criteria, intervention (dosing/procedure), comparator arms, outcomes, randomization ('randomly assigned'), blinding rationale, statistical methods (chi-square, repeated-measures ANOVA), and results are all explicitly described. No sample-size/power justification is given anywhere. No adverse-event, safety, or harms section or statement appears in the article. No funding source or conflict-of-interest statement appears (only a personal-thanks acknowledgment to colleagues). n_met=11, below the 13-of-14 threshold, so MethodologyDescribedYN=0.

article.BaseStatus: The article reports 'years of problem drinking' (mean 8.15) and describes patients as clinic-referred alcoholics, some of 'skid row' background, but gives no explicit severity classification (e.g., no AUD severity score, no clinician-rated severity). Coded '.' rather than guessing a band.
article.RaceEthnicity_BIPOCPercent: Article reports no race or ethnicity data anywhere. Coded '.'.
article.Country_USvsNonUS: Study conducted at the London Clinic, Alcoholism and Drug Addiction Research Foundation, London, Ontario, Canada. Coded 'NonUS'.
article.ConfoundYN: Authors report a chi-square comparison of the four final groups on age, sex, referral source, severity of drinking, marital status, education, employment, and accommodation to establish baseline homogeneity -- a substantive assessment of potential confounders across arms. Coded 1.
article.PrimaryCare: No aspect of recruitment, intervention delivery, or follow-up is described as occurring through primary-care settings or providers; the study is entirely clinic/hospital-based. Coded 0.
article.ValidatedScaleMeasYN: Table 3 lists baseline psychometrics (Differential Personality Inventory, Quick/IQ Test, Hidden Figures Test, Straus-Bacon Social Stability Index) used to characterize the sample at intake, not as pre/post outcome measures. The actual outcome criteria in Table 4 (abstinence, drinking practices, consequences, attitudes, employment, accommodation, social relations, marital status) are drawn from the clinic's own intake/follow-up questionnaire, not a named validated instrument. Coded 0.
article.SocioeconomicStatusYN: Text explicitly describes the clinic population as drawn 'largely from a lower- to middle-class population' and Table 3 reports a quantified 'Social class' variable (mean 3.53, SD 0.93). Coded 1.
article.RecruitmentRepresentYN: Patients were drawn from routine clinic contacts (self-referred or physician/agency-referred, ~220 intakes/year), not recruited via advertisement for a research volunteer pool, so recruitment itself reflects the clinic's real-world caseload. Note, however, that the final 95-patient scheme was reached after a large sequential exclusion cascade (337 initial contacts -> 95 final, Table 1/2), so the analyzed sample is more selected than the recruitment source alone suggests.
article.InterventionTherapy: Groups 2 and 3 (n=25, n=22) received the drug with an active co-therapist present for structured interaction; group 4 (n=25) received routine individual/group/milieu therapy. Group 1 (n=23) received LSD with only a supportive nurse present, no therapist. Coded 1 at the study level because therapy/counseling beyond drug administration alone was part of the design for 3 of 4 arms, but this does not apply uniformly to Group 1.
article.MentalHealthChangeMeasured: The Discussion section narratively reports that some patients described 'lessening of tension, depression, irritability, and isolation' after the drug session, but this is an unstructured post-session subjective account, not a formal pre/post mental-health outcome measure tracked with statistics in Table 4 (which covers only drinking, employment, accommodation, social relations, and marital status). Coded 0.
article.HarmsAssessed: The article contains no adverse-event, safety, or side-effects section, table, or explicit statement anywhere -- not in Methods, Results, or Discussion. Mentions of a Posey restraint belt and post-session chlorpromazine/Tuinal sedation are described as routine session-management procedure, not as treatment of, or assessment for, adverse reactions. Per the cardinal AE rule, this reads as the authors never looking rather than as a 'no AEs occurred' finding, so SafetyReported='N' and HarmsAssessed=0 (not 1).
article.AnyAEReported / NumDistinctAEs / NPartic: All coded 'NA' as the mandatory cascade from SafetyReported='N' (article silent on AEs/safety entirely); AE_denominator is coded '.' per the rule that this field is never 'NA'.
article.Comparator: Two comparator conditions exist: Group 3, an active-drug control (IV sodium amobarbital + methamphetamine with therapist), and Group 4, a no-drug routine-care control (individual/group/milieu therapy, no hospitalization). Coded 1.
article.Pos Result Y/N: All four groups, including the LSD arms, improved significantly pre-to-post on most drinking indices, but the ANOVA between-groups comparison was NS on every criterion (Table 4) -- the study's own conclusion is that LSD conferred 'no evident advantages over more conventional modes of therapy' and 'lends no support to the claims made for the efficacy of LSD treatment.' Coded 0 (null/negative) because the relevant test is the LSD-vs-comparator difference, which was null.
article.Followup in months: Text states a 'one-year follow-up' made 'as close to the 12-month mark as possible' from the patient's entry into the scheme. Treatment (a single hospital session) occurred shortly after intake, so the entry-based and end-of-treatment horizons do not differ materially here. Coded 12.
article.EligibleYN: (a) Prospectively planned trial: 95 patients enrolled under a defined protocol, randomly assigned to 4 arms, with prospective 12-month outcome assessment -- passes. (b) SUD outcome reported: abstinence, drinking practices, consequences of drinking, and attitudes toward drinking are all explicitly measured pre/post -- passes. Both criteria met, EligibleYN='Y'.

config_proposal.note: The primary between-groups comparison (LSD vs. active-drug and no-drug controls) on the primary drinking/abstinence outcome is reported only as the qualitative tag 'NS' in Table 4, with no F-value, t-value, mean difference, or other convertible statistic anywhere in the article. No defensible d/g/eta_p/F/chi2/OR/RR conversion is possible.
config_proposal.tier2_basis: All four arms (two LSD arms, an active-drug control, and a no-drug routine-care control) showed statistically significant pre-to-post improvement on drinking indices (p<.01 to p<.10), but the ANOVA between-groups test was non-significant on every criterion in Table 4, and the authors explicitly conclude LSD conferred no advantage over the comparator conditions -- a null differential-effect result rather than a negative one.
